title: Long-term effects of weight-reducing diets in people with hypertension
authors: Semlitsch T, Krenn C, Jeitler K, Berghold A, Horvath K, Siebenhofer A
population: Eight randomised trials of at least 24 weeks comparing weight-reducing diets with no dietary intervention in adults with primary hypertension, mean age 45 to 66 years; search to April 2020
funder: Internal sources: Medical University of Graz, Austria (salary, office space, computer support, library resources); Institute of General Practice, Goethe University Frankfurt, Germany (salary). External sources: no sources of support supplied.
authorConflicts: Siebenhofer, Jeitler and Horvath contributed to an IQWiG report on non-drug treatment of hypertension by weight reduction; the other authors report none.
result: No trial included mortality as a predefined outcome and none evaluated adverse events as defined in the protocol. One trial found a lower risk of a combined end point of reinstated antihypertensive therapy and severe cardiovascular complications (hazard ratio 0.70, 95% CI 0.57 to 0.87). Systolic pressure -4.5 mm Hg (-7.2 to -1.8) and diastolic -3.2 mm Hg (-4.8 to -1.5) (3 trials, 731 participants; low certainty); body weight -4.0 kg (-4.8 to -3.2; 5 trials, 880; high certainty). The authors conclude that whether weight loss reduces mortality and morbidity is unknown.
